title: FBISE Section A Board Examination Simulator 10 (Full-Book Board Simulator III)
subject: english-10

questions.question: Choose the correct passive voice: 'They will have finished the bridge by December.'

options.A: The bridge will have been finished by them by December.
options.B: The bridge will be finished by them by December.
options.C: The bridge would have been finished by them by December.
options.D: The bridge will has been finished by them by December.

questions.explanation: Future perfect active ('will have finished') changes to 'will have been + past participle' ('will have been finished').

questions.question: Choose the correct verb form: 'Each of the participants ___ awarded a certificate.'
questions.explanation: 'Each' is an indefinite distributive pronoun that strictly takes a singular verb ('was awarded').

questions.question: Identify the verbal: 'We watched the eagle *soar* above the mountains.'
questions.explanation: Verbs of perception like 'watch', 'see', and 'hear' take a bare infinitive ('soar') when describing the perceived action.

questions.question: Identify the grammatical role of the underlined clause: 'The problem is *that we have run out of funds*.'
questions.explanation: 'that we have run out of funds' follows the copular verb 'is' and defines the subject 'The problem', functioning as a subject complement Noun Clause.

questions.question: Complete the sentence: 'Unless you ___ your ticket, you cannot board the train.'
questions.explanation: 'Unless' already means 'if not'; therefore, it takes an affirmative simple present verb ('show') without double negatives.

questions.question: Choose the correct pronoun: 'Between you and ___, there should be no misunderstandings.'
questions.explanation: 'Between' is a preposition, and prepositions strictly govern objective case pronouns ('between you and me', not 'between you and I').

questions.question: Identify the type of sentence: 'Do or die.'
questions.explanation: Two imperative independent clauses ('Do' and 'die') connected by coordinating conjunction 'or' form a Compound Sentence.

questions.question: Choose the appropriate preposition: 'He jumped ___ the swimming pool to rescue the child.'
questions.explanation: 'Into' conveys dynamic motion from outside to an interior enclosed space, unlike the static preposition 'in'.

questions.question: What is the true reality and core essence of the wind according to the poem 'Peace'?

options.A: Gentle, silent whisper and everlasting eternal peace

questions.explanation: The poetess concludes that the destructive storm is ephemeral; the true, eternal reality of the wind is gentle whispers and serene peace.

questions.question: She says, "I love reading novels." Choose the correct indirect speech:

options.A: She says that she loved reading novels.
options.B: She says that she loves reading novels.
options.C: She said that she loves reading novels.
options.D: She says that she had loved reading novels.

questions.explanation: When the reporting verb is in the present tense ('says') or future tense, the tense of the reported speech does NOT change ('loves reading novels').

questions.question: Choose the correct passive voice of the sentence with prepositional verb: 'They laughed at the clown.'

options.A: The clown was laughed at by them.
options.B: The clown was laughed by them.
options.C: The clown had been laughed at by them.

questions.explanation: In prepositional verbs ('laughed at'), the preposition must be retained alongside the past participle in passive voice ('was laughed at by them').

questions.question: Select the correct sentence with proper subject-verb agreement:

options.A: The quality of these mangoes is exceptional.
options.B: The quality of these mangoes are exceptional.
options.C: The quality of these mangoes were exceptional.
options.D: The quality of these mangoes have been exceptional.

questions.explanation: The subject is the singular head noun 'The quality' (not the plural modifier 'mangoes'), so it takes the singular verb 'is'.

questions.question: Identify the function of the underlined infinitive: '*To forgive* is a noble virtue.'
questions.explanation: 'To forgive' stands at the beginning of the clause as the grammatical subject of the linking verb 'is'.

questions.question: Identify the underlined part: 'He drove the car *at a breakneck speed*.'
questions.explanation: 'at a breakneck speed' answers 'How did he drive?' without a finite verb, functioning as an Adverb Phrase of Manner.

questions.question: Choose the modal for polite request: '*Would* you mind closing the window?'
questions.explanation: 'Would you mind...' is a standard idiomatic formula for making a courteous, polite request.
